messages:
Jess: Quick sync — I'm proposing we split the autoscaler responsibilities: operator handles immediate node lifecycle & graceful drain, control-plane owns predictive headroom (warmup credits). Current monolith oscillates under bursty patterns. Thoughts?

Kai: +1. Operator should be reactive, CP does forecasting. Biggest open: safe transfer of "admission tokens" (who can prewarm & when). :eyes:

Marta: We've toyed with a token-bucket bank idea. CP mints tenant-scoped warmup credits based on moving avg and forecasts. Operator redeems credits to create prewarmed nodes. If credits exhausted -> operator falls back to reactive coldstart. This prevents double-counting warmups.

Devon: Important callout — billing & cost ownership. Warmup nodes must be tagged to tenant so finance can attribute idle GPU hours. Otherwise orgs will push back.

Jess: Agreed re: tagging. Also want admission circuit tied to SLOs: when predictive confidence low, operator should prefer cheaper model variants or degraded routing rather than risk high cost.

Kai: Implementation sketch (very rough):
```
warmup_policy:
  window: 5m
  credit_rate: function(usage_history) -> credits_per_min
operator_api:
  claim(warmup_id) -> {node_id, lease_ttl}
  release(node_id)
  heartbeat(node_id)
```

Kai: Claim must be idempotent and provide a lease to avoid double-assignment if operator crashes.

Marta: +1. Use optimistic locking on warmup_id and lease_ttl > expected prewarm time to avoid races. Also keep a short reclaim window for leaked leases.

Devon: Another edge: multi-region tenants. CP should issue region-scoped credits; operator redeems local ones. If local empty, fallback to nearest region per policy (latency vs cost tradeoff).

Jess: Rollout idea: feature-flag CP to emit credits in read-only mode (no operator consumption) so we can validate prediction signals, then flip operator to consume credits in canary.

runtime-bot: autoscaler-v3 canary deployed to staging :rocket: (tests running)

Kai: Rollout plan: 1) CP read-only credits for 48h 2) operator claim API PR + canary with 2 tenants 24h 3) monitor fallback_rate, headroom_utilization, cost_tagging metrics.

Jess: Action items: 1) PR operator claim API (Kai) 2) CP headroom service proto (Marta) 3) billing tagging + SLO dashboard (Devon & Sam) 4) Canary checklist (Kai).

Sam: I'll add dashboard panels: headroom_available, credits_consumed, fallback_rate, prewarm_idle_hours. Will wire cost tagging into billing pipeline.

Marta: One more: we should define a tight SLA for lease_ttl expiration semantics and a debug endpoint to list outstanding warmup_ids and their owners. Helpful during canary.

Jess: Yep. Also include a metric for "predictive_confidence" so we can automatically reduce credit issuance if confidence drops.

Kai: Sounds good. I'll open the operator API PR today. :thumbsup:

Devon: I can draft the billing tagging spec and region-fallback policy later today.

Jess: Thanks all. If anyone sees a critical gap call it out here — otherwise we track in the PRs.

Marta: minor nit — let's name credits something non-confusing (e.g., "prewarm_tokens") to avoid overlap with rate-limiting tokens.

Jess: Good point. We'll standardize naming in the proto.

Sam: Ack.

Kai: filing next steps in the RFC follow-up doc.

Jess: End of thread for now. :v:
